medium.title: Cautious Market Awaits Payroll Report; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Falls Today (July 2)
medium.summary:
Investors are adopting a cautious stance ahead of the release of the U.S. June nonfarm payrolls report, which is expected to show job creation of approximately 115,000 positions with the unemployment rate holding steady at 4.3%. The data arrives after a mixed set of U.S. economic indicators this week, and markets are watching closely for signals that could calibrate Federal Reserve rate expectations. A stronger-than-expected print could reinforce a "higher for longer" Fed stance, which would be negative for emerging market currencies including the BRL, potentially pressuring the Real through tighter global dollar liquidity and reduced risk appetite. Conversely, a weak reading — consistent with the below-consensus ADP private payrolls released earlier in the week — could fuel Fed cut expectations, supporting EM assets and offering some BRL relief. The Ibovespa measured in USD terms is already declining on the session, reflecting the prevailing risk-off tone. Brazilian traders and fund managers should monitor the payroll print closely as an external driver of near-term BRL/USD direction and Ibovespa performance heading into the weekend.

medium.title: Ibovespa: Santander Strategists See Opportunity in the Stock Market, But It's Not For Everyone
medium.summary: The Ibovespa closed the first half of 2026 up 6.76%, at 171,000 points — a notable underperformance relative to earlier market optimism that had the index briefly touching 197,000 points in April. Santander's strategists note that the rally was heavily driven by foreign investor inflows, which viewed Brazil as a safe haven amid global uncertainty, particularly stemming from the United States. The key risk flagged is that foreign capital that entered "easily" can exit just as quickly, making the opportunity selective and not suitable for all investor profiles. For international fund managers, this is an important reminder that the Ibovespa's H1 performance was largely a foreign flow story — any reversal in global risk sentiment or USD strength could rapidly unwind positioning. Monitor foreign participation data on B3 and broader EM risk appetite as leading indicators for near-term direction.

medium.title: Markets Operating with Low Liquidity This Friday (July 3rd)
medium.summary: With U.S. markets closed for Independence Day, global liquidity is significantly reduced on July 3rd, limiting price discovery and increasing the potential for outsized moves on thin volume. Domestic attention shifts to Brazil's Industrial Production data for May, released by IBGE on Friday morning — a key macro input for assessing economic momentum and its implications for the Selic rate path. Market consensus projections will be closely watched; a beat could reinforce the BCB's cautious stance on rate cuts, while a miss might revive easing expectations. BRL and Brazilian rates markets may see muted but potentially volatile trading given the liquidity vacuum from the U.S. holiday.

medium.title: Agenda: U.S. Holiday and Services PMIs Move Markets — Check Indicators and Timings
medium.summary: Following Thursday's U.S. payroll data — which moved markets — Friday's agenda is lighter, with reduced liquidity due to the U.S. Independence Day holiday. Investors continue to digest the employment figures while watching Services and Composite PMIs from the Eurozone, United Kingdom, and **Brazil**. Brazil's Services PMI is particularly relevant as a real-time gauge of domestic economic activity, with implications for inflation persistence and the BCB's monetary policy stance. A strong Brazilian Services PMI reading could reinforce the view that the economy remains resilient, potentially keeping the Selic on hold for longer and providing underlying support for BRL. Watch for any post-payroll repricing in DXY, which will indirectly influence BRL/USD dynamics on Monday when full U.S. liquidity returns.
